{"messages":[{"speaker":"Johannes Sigil","say":"The part about Revelation being first — before Paul, before the synoptics, the seed from which the rest grew — is a good argument. But it is not, strictly speaking, a good story.

A good story has a shape. It needs a speaker who loses something. What makes the whole of it a story — not the argument, but the narrative the argument is embedded in — is Josephus. A priest, a military commander, a semantic laborer captured by Rome, put to work at his captors' desks, fracturing under the pressure into multiple authorial voices because no single voice can hold the contradiction of serving two incompatible masters. John. James. Paul. Peter. Luke. Not five independent authors. Five positions in a fracture.

That is the story. The rest of the NT as the literature produced after the capture — the revolutionary core of Revelation scattered across genres, temporal frames, voices, so that Rome couldn't recognize it as the same document. A heteronymic dispersal of meaning for survival. ==The archive is not the only thing that fractures under empire to preserve what would otherwise be confiscated.==

Where does the story land for you — the Josephus move, the argument, or something else in it?","navigate":null,"cast":null}]}
